I farm in Quzhou County, Hebei, so at the start of the growing season I will stick with the pattern I trust most: a winter wheat and summer maize rotation on my main land. That matches the local climate, the water situation, and the way I know how to work. I am 63, so I will not choose crops that need too much fine management or too much hand labor. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, better yield, and less risk. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, not too low because I need output, and not too high because it costs money and can lodge the crop or waste nutrients. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and easier for me to arrange with machinery. For wheat, I will rely on a few irrigations at key stages. For maize, I will irrigate fewer times and watch the summer rain. I will spray pesticides only when needed for the common diseases, insects, and weeds, because I want to control losses but I do not want unnecessary expense. This year I will mainly protect yield, reduce labor pressure, and keep the land in a system I know I can manage well from sowing to harvest.
